counterfactual_missing_items: No mention of family history of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
Lack of leptomeningeal angiomatosis on imaging studies
No obvious abnormalities on Cranial CT at 2 years
decisive_items: repeated right-sided epistaxis without obvious trauma
Multiple small capillary malformations on trunk (hyperpigmented)
response.rationale: R1 is the champion because it has the most comprehensive support from the vignette, including repeated epistaxis, vascular malformation, and capillary malformations. R5 is the runner-up because it also has some support from the vignette, but the lack of leptomeningeal angiomatosis on imaging studies makes it less likely.

rejected.why: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome is less likely due to the lack of limb hypertrophy and the presence of repeated epistaxis, which is more consistent with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
PHACE syndrome is less likely due to the lack of large facial hemangioma and the presence of repeated epistaxis, which is more consistent with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is less likely due to the lack of significant joint hypermobility and skin hyperextensibility, and the presence of repeated epistaxis and vascular malformation, which are more consistent with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
